title.value: Spectral Regularization: an Inductive Bias for Sequence Modeling
title.justification: The title of the paper is provided at the beginning: 'Spectral Regularization: an Inductive Bias for Sequence Modeling'. It accurately reflects the main focus of the paper.
title.quote: Spectral Regularization: an Inductive Bias for Sequence Modeling

extractions.description: This paper presents a spectral regularization technique for sequence modeling by attaching a unique inductive bias based on the Chomsky hierarchy. Through the use of the trace norm of the Hankel matrix, the approach encourages learning of models approximating regular grammars. The paper introduces a stochastic estimator for the trace norm and validates the approach through experiments with Tomita grammars.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper's primary focus is on applying spectral regularization to sequence modeling, with no direct reference to sustainable development issues such as climate change or ecological sustainability.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: This paper presents a spectral regularization technique, which attaches a unique inductive bias to sequence modeling based on an intuitive concept of simplicity defined in the Chomsky hierarchy.

secondary_sub_categories.quote: Spectral regularization can thus incorporate a natural inductive bias towards regular functions in the training of any black-box differentiable model.

applications.quote: While there are many natural notions of simplicity for functions defined over vector spaces, defining a notion of simplicity suited for functions defined over sequences can be more tedious due to the discrete and sequential nature of the data.
